blocks.text: 52 Morning Prayer for the New Year 52
אתה

Thou art our God in heaven and on earth.
Mighty and awe-inspiring distinguished among myriads.
He spoke and it came to pass, He commanded, then were they created.
His memory is forever, He lives in all eternity.
Pure is His gaze, He is enthroned in mystery.
His crown is salvation, His robe is righteousness.
His cloak is zeal, He is girded with retribution.
His mystery is equity, His counsel faith.
His work is truth, He is just and upright.
He is close to those who call Him in truth, lofty and exalted.
He resides in the clouds and suspends the earth in space.
uncertainties: Printed in two columns that do not align line for line. Pairing is reconstructed from the Hebrew; the visual rows are offset after line 3.

blocks.text: Living, enduring, awe-inspiring, lofty and holy.
On Sabbath we say שמו מפארים etc., as below.
uncertainties: Italic; the Hebrew words are embedded

blocks.text: תעיר
Thou dost rise and let the trumpet sound to destroy every evil doer, and Thou art sanctified by those who know how to sound the Teruah, Holy One.
אדרת

The glorious realm, how has it been cast down and not yet been restored to rule. It swore allegiance to Bel, it followed him against the law. Thus there gained dominion over it a mighty alien realm, until God's realm will once again appear. It has burned my sanctuary, it has crushed my upright
uncertainties: There is a stray overline mark above 'it' after 'Bel,'. It is probably a print artifact, not punctuation.
The text continues on the next page.

blocks.text: On Sabbath.
uncertainties: Below a horizontal rule; italic

blocks.text: שמו
His Name is praised by the community of His portion, His praise is proclaimed by the holy Erelim and in His sanctuary everything utters glory of the Holy One.
שומרי

Those who observe His commandments will yet return to the fortress, those who fear Him, speak to one another in purity and bliss, and the Lord has listened and heard and it is inscribed in the book of remembrance, the Holy One.
שפרו
Improve your deeds that the covenant may not be broken, He who has adorned the skies, will hear your cry, and it will be more pleasing than the sacrifice of oxen to the Lord the Holy One.

notes: Scope: per the instructions, s132 and s133 were read as whole pages. Neither has a rule-bounded section to skip at the top. The band images overlapped (the פְּעֻלָּתוֹ line and the לַבֵּל/שַׁפְּרוּ lines appear twice); I have recorded those words only once.

Sections on s132: an ark-opening rubric; אתה הוא אלהינו (alphabetical acrostic ע״ס א״ב, two columns) with refrain חי וקים; ark-closing rubric; a Shabbat substitution rubric; a Metz custom rubric; תעיר ותריע (חו״ק); the attribution (Kalir acrostic); אדרת ממלכה (ק׳), first part only, continuing past the page; then below the rule the Shabbat alternative שמו מפארים, שומרי מצותיו, שפרו מעשיכם (each חו״ק).

Printed conditional alternatives: (1) In Frankfurt am Main (פפד״ם) אתה הוא אלהינו is omitted and the service starts with תעיר ותריע. (2) On Shabbat, שמו מפארים is said in its place (the English says 'On Sabbath we say שמו מפארים etc.'). (3) The Metz (ק״ק מיץ) custom omits something before תריע; the word is uncertain.
Embedded citations, not marked in print: Malachi 3:16 (ויקשב יי וישמע ויכתב ספר זכרון) in שומרי; Psalms 69:32 (ותיטב ליי משור פר) in שפרו.

Possible source issues, transcribed as printed: הָשְׁלָכָה (expected הֻשְׁלָכָה) and the catchword's first letter ז/ו (expected זְבוּלִי). Both are pointing or letter readings to check at higher resolution, not confirmed typos.
No Biblical cantillation marks are visible on these pages. Possible meteg marks are noted per block and are not confirmed.
The English page does not translate the Hebrew rubrics about Frankfurt, opening and closing the ark, Metz, or the Kalir attribution. They are left out as instructed.
